chapter: Brass bands, Buddy Petit and horns
title: Chasing Buddy to get the horn back
summary: A long story of lending Buddy his horn, hunting him down at his house, and a night out with Billy Marrero and a found pocketbook.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I learned something. I learned something to play one. He had a job at the, at the cooperatives. And, uh, his horn broke. He never had no good horn. He said, the only last one, he was moved to Dave. He thought he bought a horn. And, uh, he said, uh, Joe. I said, what you want? I said, you want a horn, I guess. I said, before he came out, he said, yeah, I'm going to borrow your horn. I said, I listen to Buddy, I'm going to lend him a horn. I said, I'm going to keep two. Right there's three, sometimes two. I kept one, something happened to one, I'll get the other one. He said, I said, I'm going to do it a week, yeah? He said, you get one. He said, well, it's wonderful, one day. I said, I'll tell you, keep it the whole week. I knew it. He said, I knew it. I knew you'd have seen that. And, uh, he kept it. He played it. He played it. At the common hall, they had a good crowd, packed. And the next night, it was packed again. The next night, uh, he played, uh, he played some, he played some, a white horse. I forgot the name of the horse, and I played that. And, uh, so that side, that side, I went to get the horn. That's, that, uh, that's Monday. Monday, I went to get the horn. And he said, man, I'm playing, y'all. I'm playing all the way. I said, I know you're playing. You're playing, but you ain't got no horn. He said, I was cutting over the horn right away on the other day. He said, I, I, I, I want to buy a horn. I said, you can't buy that horn, man. He said, you crazy? That was a good horn, too, you know? He said, well, let me see what you're talking about. I ain't got nothing to you at all, brother. I said, I thought, brother. I said, I, after I stood there, I said, I said, I'm gonna, you can play it one more night with it. I said, I'll let you complete, you're gonna play the con and horn. I said, yeah. I said, all right, go ahead, you can use the con and horn. And one more night, Tuesday, I'll come and get it. I said, I ain't gonna depend on you bringing it, because you said it, you never come. I'm gonna come get it. I went there that night, and I said, bummer, I had to call him. He said, bummer, all my days. And, uh, I went, I went there, and I knocked, by nine o'clock. I could see him peeping, you know, through the blinds, his wife. I see it, I look at her, I see her playing some tricks, and I, it wouldn't come out of it right away, you know. I hit it again. I said, who is that, that, who I was before I would say that? I didn't see that, I didn't see that. I see them. I was like, I'm going to go, and, uh, he said, uh, buddy, you know, buddy ain't coming yet? I said, what? Cut him off, wouldn't give him a chance to. I said, ain't he coming yet? Since last night? She said, no, ain't he. I said, I don't hear him telling you nothing. He said, all right. I'll tell him, though, when he come out, he might come to see him all the time. He was there, he was there, yeah. I said, listen, I got, I got kind of hot. He wouldn't say nothing, I was going to stand at the corner, I stayed all night. I watched him. I watched him, I sat right at the corner, I could see him. He had to come out of guard, if you want to go out, he had to jump him down. A lot of times, he stayed right in the middle of the block. And, uh, if you want to go out the other way. And, so I, I, I got off the corner where he couldn't see me. I got off the corner, I got, right, right, you know, in the point, like, you know, I watched. I watched. I said, listen, I'll be better go see you back home, I said. I got up my watch. I said, Lily, I didn't knock, I hollered, I called Lily. He said, looking through the block, I could see you. He said, but he couldn't see me. I said, how you know, you can't see me, can you? He said, yeah, yeah, I see you. I see you sitting at the corner while I was looking like, you know, long give way on and stuff. I said, yeah. I said, I wasn't sitting there for long. Oh, yeah, you would. He said, yeah. I said, you call that long? While I talked to him, buddy slipped, slipped him under a table, the kind of table that had him. He kind of scooped down and went and get a fish in the corner. I was talking and I was looking at him and looking at him. I said, where I'm going? I said, coach, girl. Is he over there in that corner? I said, yeah. I said, tell the buddy to come out there. I can't see you, you can't see him, I can't see him, no. But I know that's where he went. That's where I'll go. I said, if I get up, I can see him if I get up. I'm sitting down. And he said, but he's trying to sneak out that hole that way was there. And I got up. I was talking. I wasn't looking where he was. I wasn't looking where he was. I kept looking. I looked. I said, I swear Mr. Joshua, you got a look of Butter, ain't that Butter there? She said she swear. I was going to leave him play a while with him. She said, when are you coming here? When are you coming here? Butter was sitting at the table. I said, I'm going to use that horn to watch. They ain't going to use it no more. The jerk is talking, you got to look so pitiful. I learned him again. He sat down at the table and I said, I said, what will it be? I said, Butter, what will make you alive for a life of Butter like that? I said, you make him worse. He said, I can't do nothing with him. I said, I don't know, they're totally all the same. I said, you know, I went. I left the horn there. I went home, I stopped practicing. Somebody come down. I said, him and Bill and Simon's Longfather, you know. Longfather. John Marrero. No, Billy, Billy Marrero. Billy Marrero.
Billy Marrero. Billy Marrero. Billy Marrero.

Billy. I said, come get the horn. Joe's horn. Me and Billy and the partners all the time to be together. He thought I hadn't went there yet, you know. And he said, why? Get the horn. You wouldn't care if I was going to say that I'd been back. He said, well, I see him and I bought it again. All right, he bought it again. Right there. I said, well, if there's any last juice for you, get the horn, you wouldn't care if I wasn't gonna say it out, I'll clean it back. I said, well, I see him and I borrow it again. All right, he borrowed it again. I went down, he comes back by me and he calls me and says, this brother, you see his brother? He come with the horn. I said, well, how long is this? I learned something again. I said, all right. So, that morning we went, I went out. I went to Sunfellip and Craven, they borrowed them there. That's why we used to go to the place. And drinking, eating, everything. So he said, I'm going downtown, I'm going home. And Billy said, come on, let's go. I said, I don't feel like going right now. I said, let's wait. So he said, I said, all right, I'll go. And that's where our buddy come, come, come there. But before we left, he said, yeah, he's on. It's about 10 o'clock in the day. I said, play every night. He said, yeah, that's where I know that. And he said, yeah, you're going to have me to tomorrow too? Because I got to run up on time, you don't let me say nothing. He goes out to talk me, he talked me. He looked so pitiful. I said, all right now, buddy, I'll make my home. I'll bring it, I'll let you again tomorrow. I'll let you play a flag tonight. He said, all right. So I said, I'm going. He said, you want to come south home? I'm going home now. So we went to come on down there. We stopped by his house. He said, I'm not going on fishing. He said, y'all have some money, can buy some wine and stuff. We eat. I said, I'm going home. He got no water. I eat like I want, brother. I got the shot all day. And I have a day. I wouldn't be doing nothing. I wouldn't eat nothing. I come home, I clean up. And, uh, but, but, but, but he said, God, I tell you, he's going to come. He said, uh-uh. He said, I'm going. I said, I got the pool. I got the witcher to clean and the ear, clean and everything. And I said, I'm going home right to eat. I'll be like, eat now. And, uh, but he went there. He, he, he went and bought a dime or wine. At times, he still was a bottle of dime, of course. And, think it all, him and the fuller, and I am Bruce, that trombone player. Got drunk, half drunk, and I used to get drunk quick. And, uh, so I said, come on, man, let's go.
I said, I ain't going to stay on here.

He said, wait, he's a light fish, him. He said, wait, let it come with this fish. I said, well, I said, oh. I said, Eddie might not catch nothing. He's a catch all the time, though. He said, he's going to catch him. I said, I see him. I said, I see him. I see him, I see him, I see him. I said, I'm going home. He sure. And, by the time I, I walk out the place and walk, talking with him, and Billy's talking to me, I said, I'm sure, from behind him. He came out behind me. He come home. And, when Billy got the most right down there, I see a pocketbook on the bank. I don't know what it was for you. It was shining on them big old-time pocketbooks. I had a nice two-year second constitution in the sun on the steps. And, just look right there. And, I'm looking at him, I picked it up right away. Billy didn't see any other. Shut up my cool pocket. I walked off. I said, come on, baby. He said, man, you sure walks through. I was going to tell him, by the way. He said, come on. He said, I don't want to drink no more. I said, I ain't talking much drinking. We going home. I got home. When I got around 7th and North Street. I told him. I said, you didn't see when I picked that up or hit your foot, man? He said, what? I said, look. There's 18 dollars and a lot of lots of tickets in there. I ain't going home now, no. I said, well, if I was going to walk across all year long, you see, that money I ain't going to spend. The only thing is, I bought something to eat for us. I bought something to eat. I gave him four dollars an hour. I said, well, let's go tonight about that story.
